questions.text: Convert the decimal number (147)₁₀ into its equivalent binary number:

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the 1's complement of the binary number (10110100)₂?
questions.explanation: 1's complement is obtained by bitwise inversion: 1 becomes 0, and 0 becomes 1. Inverting 10110100 yields 01001011.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In IEEE 754 Double-Precision Floating-Point standard (64 bits), how many bits are allocated to the exponent, and what is the exponent bias?
questions.explanation: IEEE 754 double precision allocates 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits (bias = 2¹⁰ - 1 = 1023), and 52 fraction/mantissa bits.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In a 2-level memory hierarchy, cache access time is 5 ns and main memory access time is 80 ns. What must be the minimum cache hit ratio to achieve an AMAT of at most 8 ns?

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: The ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) developed by Mauchly and Eckert belongs to which generation of computers?
questions.explanation: ENIAC (1946) was a pioneering First Generation computer built with over 17,000 vacuum tubes.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which type of semiconductor RAM requires periodic refresh cycles to maintain stored capacitive charge?
questions.explanation: DRAM cells store data as charge in a tiny capacitor (1 transistor + 1 capacitor) which leaks charge, necessitating periodic refresh cycles.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Convert the octal number (357)₈ into its equivalent hexadecimal representation:
questions.explanation: (357)₈ to binary: 3=011, 5=101, 7=111 => 011101111₂. Grouping in 4s from right: 1110 1111 = (EF)₁₆.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the maximum signed integer value that can be represented using an 8-bit register in 2's complement notation?
questions.explanation: An n-bit 2's complement register represents numbers from -(2ⁿ⁻¹) to +(2ⁿ⁻¹ - 1). For n=8, the range is -128 to +127.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which computer bus is unidirectional, carrying memory locations exclusively from the CPU to memory/IO devices?
questions.explanation: The Address Bus is unidirectional (CPU -> Memory/IO), while the Data Bus is bidirectional.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In a direct-mapped cache, how many blocks of main memory map to a specific cache line?

options.label: A
options.text: Multiple main memory blocks map to the same cache line via modulo indexing

options.label: B
options.text: Only exactly one block per cache line

options.label: C
options.text: Any block can map to any cache line

questions.explanation: In direct-mapped cache, Line = (Block Address) mod (Total Cache Lines). Multiple blocks share the same cache line, distinguished by Tag bits.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the BCD (Binary Coded Decimal) representation of the decimal number 89?
questions.explanation: In BCD, each decimal digit is encoded in 4-bit binary: 8 = 1000 and 9 = 1001, giving 1000 1001.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which magnetic storage device allows purely sequential (serial) access to stored records?
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape is a sequential access medium (must wind through preceding data); disks and SSDs provide direct/random access.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A byte-addressable computer system has a 32-bit physical address. If the cache size is 64 KB with 32-byte block size in a 4-way set associative cache, how many tag bits are required?
questions.explanation: Block offset = log2(32) = 5 bits. Cache lines = 64KB / 32B = 2048 lines. Sets = 2048 / 4 = 512 sets => Set index = log2(512) = 9 bits. Tag bits = 32 - (9 + 5) = 18 bits.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Computers
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the ASCII character code value for uppercase letter 'A' in decimal?
questions.explanation: In 7-bit ASCII: 'A' = 65, 'Z' = 90, lowercase 'a' = 97, 'z' = 122, digit '0' = 48.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Which logic gates are referred to as 'Universal Logic Gates' because any Boolean function can be implemented using them alone?
questions.explanation: NAND and NOR gates are universal gates capable of realizing NOT, AND, and OR operations independently.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: According to De Morgan's Law, the Boolean expression (A + B)' is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: De Morgan's first theorem states: (A + B)' = A' . B'. De Morgan's second theorem states: (A . B)' = A' + B'.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A Full Adder combinational circuit can be constructed using:

options.label: A
options.text: Two Half Adders and One OR gate

options.label: B
options.text: Two Half Adders and One AND gate

options.label: C
options.text: One Half Adder and Two OR gates

questions.explanation: A Full Adder adds 3 bits (A, B, Cin). It consists of two Half Adders (generating intermediate sums and carries) and an OR gate combining the carry outputs.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: In a JK Flip-Flop, what happens when both J and K inputs are set to logic HIGH (J=1, K=1) during a clock pulse?
questions.explanation: When J=1 and K=1, the JK flip-flop toggles its output state (solves the indeterminate state problem of the SR flip-flop).

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: How many select input lines are required for a 16-to-1 Multiplexer (MUX)?
questions.explanation: A multiplexer with 2ⁿ data inputs requires n select lines. Since 16 = 2⁴, 4 select lines are required.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which flip-flop eliminates the race-around condition by ensuring the next state always equals the data input D?
questions.explanation: A D flip-flop transfers its D input directly to output Q on the clock trigger (Q(next) = D), widely used in shift registers.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: In Morris Mano's basic computer architecture, what are the four phases of the instruction cycle in order?

options.label: A
options.text: Fetch Instruction $\to$ Decode Instruction $\to$ Read Effective Address $\to$ Execute Instruction

questions.explanation: The instruction cycle phases are: 1. Fetch instruction from memory into IR; 2. Decode instruction; 3. Read effective address (if indirect); 4. Execute.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which addressing mode specifies the operand directly within the instruction itself (e.g., ADDI R1, #5)?
questions.explanation: In Immediate addressing mode, the operand is part of the instruction itself, requiring no memory access to fetch the data.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Relative Addressing Mode, the effective address of the operand is calculated by adding the address field to the contents of:
questions.explanation: Relative addressing computes Effective Address = PC + Address Offset, commonly used in branch and jump instructions.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A 5-stage non-pipelined processor executes an instruction in 50 ns. If a 5-stage pipelined version has a clock cycle of 11 ns (due to 1 ns latch delay), what is the speedup for executing 1000 instructions?
questions.explanation: Non-pipelined time = 1000 * 50 ns = 50,000 ns. Pipelined time = (k + n - 1) * cycle = (5 + 1000 - 1) * 11 ns = 1004 * 11 = 11,044 ns. Speedup = 50,000 / 11,044 ≈ 4.527.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: The minimal Sum of Products (SOP) form of the Boolean expression F = A'B + AB is:

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: How many 3-to-8 line decoders with enable inputs are needed to construct a 4-to-16 line decoder?

options.label: A
options.text: Two 3-to-8 decoders (and one inverter for enable)

questions.explanation: Using the 4th bit to drive the active-high/active-low enable lines directly (with one inverter), two 3-to-8 decoders form a 4-to-16 decoder.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Direct Memory Access (DMA) data transfer bypasses which component to achieve high-speed bulk data movement between disk and RAM?
questions.explanation: DMA controllers transfer data directly between I/O peripherals and main memory without burdening the CPU with per-byte interrupts.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: An interrupt that cannot be masked or ignored by software instructions is called a:
questions.text_alt: ಸಾಫ್ಟ್‌ವೇರ್ ಮೂಲಕ ನಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಿಸಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಾಗದ ಅತ್ಯುನ್ನತ ಆದ್ಯತೆಯ ಇಂಟರಪ್ಟ್ ಯಾವುದು?
questions.explanation: Non-Maskable Interrupts (like power failure, bus parity errors) have the highest priority and cannot be disabled by CLI instructions.

questions.subject: Digital Logic & Organization
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In a 4-variable Karnaugh Map (K-Map), grouping a block of 8 adjacent cells (an octet) eliminates how many variables?
questions.explanation: In a K-map, grouping 2ⁿ cells eliminates n variables. An octet has 2³ = 8 cells, so it eliminates 3 variables.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: What will be the output of the C expression: 5 + 3 * 2 - 8 / 4?
questions.explanation: Operator precedence: * and / have higher precedence than + and -: 3*2 = 6, 8/4 = 2. Then left-to-right: 5 + 6 - 2 = 11 - 2 = 9.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In C, what is the effect of declaring a variable with the 'static' storage class inside a function?

options.label: A
options.text: The variable retains its value between function calls and has lifetime equal to program execution

options.label: B
options.text: The variable becomes global and accessible across all files

options.label: C
options.text: The variable is stored in CPU registers

questions.explanation: Static local variables are initialized once and reside in the data segment, retaining their values across successive function calls.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What does the declaration `int (*fp)(char, float);` signify in C?

options.label: A
options.text: fp is a pointer to a function taking (char, float) arguments and returning int

options.label: B
options.text: fp is a function returning a pointer to int

options.label: C
options.text: fp is an array of function pointers

questions.explanation: Parentheses around `*fp` bind the pointer to the identifier: `(*fp)` is a function pointer accepting `(char, float)` and returning `int`.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the primary difference between `malloc()` and `calloc()` functions in standard C?

options.label: A
options.text: calloc() initializes allocated memory bytes to zero; malloc() leaves memory uninitialized (garbage values)

options.label: B
options.text: malloc() allocates from heap, calloc() allocates from stack

options.label: C
options.text: malloc() takes two arguments, calloc() takes one

options.label: D
options.text: calloc() cannot be freed using free()

questions.explanation: calloc(n, size) allocates contiguous memory and initializes all bits to zero; malloc(bytes) allocates uninitialized memory containing garbage.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: In C++, dynamic polymorphism (late binding) is achieved using which mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Virtual functions and base class pointers/references

questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism in C++ is implemented via virtual functions, where the compiler sets up a vtable and vptr to resolve calls at runtime.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A class containing at least one pure virtual function (e.g., `virtual void draw() = 0;`) is known as:
questions.explanation: An abstract class contains one or more pure virtual functions (`= 0`) and cannot be directly instantiated.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Why should a base class destructor always be declared as `virtual` when deleting derived objects via base pointers?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent memory leaks by ensuring the derived class destructor is invoked first

options.label: B
options.text: To make the base class abstract

options.label: D
options.text: C++ requires all destructors to be virtual

questions.explanation: If a base destructor is non-virtual, deleting a derived object via a base pointer causes undefined behavior (derived destructor never executes, leaking resources).

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which C++ feature solves the 'Diamond Problem' in multiple inheritance where a derived class inherits two copies of a common grandparent class?
questions.explanation: Virtual base classes ensure that only one shared instance of the common ancestor sub-object is included in the most derived class.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What does a pointer variable contain in C?

options.label: C
options.text: A copy of CPU register contents

questions.explanation: A pointer is a variable that stores the hexadecimal/binary memory address of another variable.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.explanation: `p` points to a[0] (10). Pointer arithmetic `p + 3` offsets 3 elements forward to &a[3]. Dereferencing `*(p + 3)` yields a[3] = 40.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What happens when a dynamically allocated block of memory is lost without being released via `free()` or `delete`?
questions.explanation: A memory leak occurs when heap memory is allocated but never deallocated and the pointer reference is lost.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which constructor is invoked when a new object is initialized as a copy of an existing object of the same class (e.g., `Point p2 = p1;`)?
questions.explanation: A copy constructor has the signature `ClassName(const ClassName &obj)` and initializes an object using an existing instance.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In C++, which operator CANNOT be overloaded?
questions.explanation: Operators that cannot be overloaded in C++ include: scope resolution `::`, member selection `.`, pointer-to-member `.*`, and ternary `?:`.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the size of a `union` in C?

options.label: A
options.text: Equal to the size of its largest member

options.label: B
options.text: Sum of sizes of all its members

questions.explanation: All members of a union share the same memory location; hence the union's size is determined by its largest data member.

questions.subject: Programming with C & C++
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In C++, when an exception is thrown inside a `try` block, what mechanism ensures that local stack objects are properly destructed in reverse order of construction?
questions.explanation: Stack Unwinding is the runtime process that exits scopes and executes destructors of local automatic objects until an appropriate catch block is found.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Which data structure operates on the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) operational principle?
questions.explanation: A Stack operates on LIFO (Last-In First-Out), where the last inserted element is the first removed (push/pop at top).

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the postfix evaluation result of the expression: `6 3 2 + * 5 -`?
questions.explanation: Evaluation: 3 2 + = 5. Then 6 * 5 = 30. Then 30 - 5 = 25.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In a Circular Queue of size N implemented using an array, what condition indicates that the queue is completely full?
questions.explanation: In a circular queue, full condition is `(rear + 1) % N == front`; empty condition is `front == rear` (or front == -1).

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort algorithm?
questions.explanation: QuickSort has average complexity O(n log n), but degrades to worst-case O(n²) when the partition is unbalanced (e.g. array already sorted).

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which sorting algorithm guarantees O(n log n) time complexity in the worst case, best case, and average case, while requiring O(n) auxiliary space?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort consistently divides the array in half and merges, guaranteeing O(n log n) in all cases with O(n) auxiliary space.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In-order traversal of a valid Binary Search Tree (BST) produces keys in:
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits (Left, Root, Right). In a BST, Left < Root < Right, so in-order produces sorted ascending keys.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the defining balance factor property of an AVL tree for every node?
questions.explanation: An AVL tree is a self-balancing BST where the balance factor (Height(Left) - Height(Right)) of every node must be -1, 0, or +1.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Dijkstra's Single-Source Shortest Path algorithm fails to produce correct results in graphs containing:
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's greedy choice assumes adding an edge never decreases path cost, so it fails on negative weight edges (Bellman-Ford is used instead).

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which algorithmic design paradigm is used by Kruskal's algorithm to construct a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)?
questions.explanation: Kruskal's algorithm sorts edges by weight and greedily selects the minimum-weight edge that does not form a cycle (using Disjoint Set Union).

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the time complexity to insert a new node at the beginning (head) of a Singly Linked List?
questions.explanation: Inserting at head requires allocating a node, setting `newNode->next = head`, and `head = newNode`, executing in O(1) constant time.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Breadth-First Search (BFS) graph traversal standardly uses which data structure?
questions.explanation: BFS explores level by level using a FIFO Queue; Depth-First Search (DFS) uses a LIFO Stack (or recursion).

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of depth (height) h, where root is at level 0?
questions.explanation: Max nodes = 2⁰ + 2¹ + ... + 2ʰ = 2^(h+1) - 1. For height h=3, max nodes = 2⁴ - 1 = 15.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Floyd's Cycle-Finding algorithm (tortoise and hare) detects a loop in a linked list in:

options.label: A
options.text: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space

options.label: C
options.text: O(n log n) time and O(1) space

questions.explanation: Floyd's algorithm advances slow pointer by 1 step and fast pointer by 2 steps; if they meet, a cycle exists, achieving O(n) time and O(1) space.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In a Max-Heap data structure with n elements, what is the time complexity to extract the maximum element?
questions.explanation: Extract-Max removes root, places last element at root, and runs Max-Heapify to restore heap property in O(log n) time.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.label: expected
questions.text: The 0/1 Knapsack problem is standardly solved using Dynamic Programming in pseudo-polynomial time of:

options.label: A
options.text: O(n * W), where n is items and W is capacity

questions.explanation: The 2D dynamic programming table `K[i][w]` requires `n` rows and `W` columns, yielding O(n * W) time complexity.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: In relational database theory, what is a single row in a database table called?
questions.explanation: In relational model terminology: Table = Relation, Row = Tuple, Column = Attribute, Number of rows = Cardinality, Number of columns = Degree.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What does Entity Integrity constraint state in the relational model?

options.label: A
options.text: No primary key attribute can contain a NULL value

options.label: B
options.text: Foreign keys must match valid primary keys

questions.explanation: Entity Integrity dictates that no component of a Primary Key can be NULL, ensuring every tuple can be uniquely identified.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: A relation is in Second Normal Form (2NF) if and only if it is in 1NF and:

options.label: A
options.text: Every non-prime attribute is fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key (no partial dependency)

options.label: D
options.text: Every determinant is a candidate key

questions.explanation: 2NF requires 1NF + elimination of partial functional dependencies (non-prime attributes cannot depend on a proper subset of a composite candidate key).

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A relation is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y:

options.label: A
options.text: Either X is a super key or Y is a prime attribute

options.label: B
options.text: X must always be a candidate key

options.label: C
options.text: Y must be a super key

questions.explanation: 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies: for X -> Y, either X is a superkey or Y is a prime attribute (part of a candidate key).

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What makes Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) strictly stronger than Third Normal Form (3NF)?

options.label: A
options.text: In BCNF, for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key (eliminating prime attribute exception)

options.label: D
options.text: BCNF applies only to non-relational databases

questions.explanation: BCNF removes the exception present in 3NF: in BCNF, every determinant X in non-trivial X -> Y must strictly be a superkey.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In SQL, which clause is used to filter aggregated group results produced by the `GROUP BY` clause?
questions.explanation: `WHERE` filters individual rows prior to grouping; `HAVING` filters aggregated groups after `GROUP BY`.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which SQL JOIN returns all rows from the left table along with matching rows from the right table, and NULLs where no match exists?
questions.explanation: LEFT OUTER JOIN preserves all tuples from the left relation, padding right attributes with NULL when the join condition fails.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: The ACID properties of database transactions ensure reliable processing. What does the 'I' in ACID stand for?
questions.explanation: ACID: Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (preserves constraints), Isolation (concurrent transactions execute independently), Durability (persists after commit).

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Two-Phase Locking (2PL) protocol, what rule guarantees serializability?

options.label: A
options.text: Once a transaction releases a lock, it can never acquire any new locks (Shrinking phase)

options.label: B
options.text: Transactions must acquire all locks before starting

questions.explanation: 2PL consists of a Growing Phase (only lock acquisitions) and a Shrinking Phase (only lock releases). No lock can be acquired after any lock is released.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What type of schedule allows transactions to read only values written by committed transactions, preventing cascading rollbacks?
questions.explanation: In a Cascadeless schedule, each transaction reads only data committed by the writing transaction, avoiding cascading aborts.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which SQL command is a Data Definition Language (DDL) command?
questions.explanation: DDL commands define schema structures: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE. DML commands manipulate data: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram, a Weak Entity Set is visually depicted by:
questions.explanation: Weak entity sets (which lack a primary key of their own) are represented by Double Rectangles, and identifying relationships by Double Diamonds.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In B+ Tree file indexing, how do leaf nodes differ from internal index nodes?

options.label: A
options.text: Leaf nodes store all actual record pointers and are linked sequentially as a doubly linked list

options.label: B
options.text: Internal nodes store all data records

options.label: D
options.text: Leaf nodes cannot be searched in O(log n)

questions.explanation: In a B+ Tree, leaf nodes contain all keys and record pointers and are linked sequentially, providing efficient range queries and sequential scans.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the difference between `DELETE` and `TRUNCATE` statements in SQL?

options.label: A
options.text: DELETE is a logged DML operation that can be rolled back; TRUNCATE is a DDL operation deallocating data pages

options.label: B
options.text: TRUNCATE removes the table definition entirely

options.label: C
options.text: DELETE cannot have a WHERE clause

questions.explanation: DELETE logs row deletions and supports WHERE and ROLLBACK; TRUNCATE deallocates extents rapidly without per-row logging and resets identity.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: The Wait-Die deadlock prevention scheme for transactions is based on timestamp ordering. If older transaction T_old requests a lock held by younger transaction T_young:

options.label: A
options.text: T_old is allowed to wait for T_young

questions.explanation: In Wait-Die: If older requests lock held by younger, older is allowed to wait. If younger requests lock held by older, younger dies (aborts).

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: The data structure maintained by the Operating System to store all control attributes of an active process (state, PC, registers, memory limits) is:
questions.explanation: The PCB (Process Control Block / Task Descriptor) stores PID, state, CPU registers, program counter, CPU scheduling, and I/O status.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives the minimum theoretical average waiting time for a given set of stationary processes?
questions.explanation: SJF is provably optimal because scheduling shorter jobs ahead reduces the cumulative waiting time for all subsequent processes.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Which four Coffman conditions are simultaneously necessary and sufficient for a Deadlock to occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait

options.label: D
options.text: Race Condition, Critical Section, Mutex, Semaphore

questions.explanation: Coffman conditions for deadlock: 1. Mutual Exclusion; 2. Hold and Wait; 3. No Preemption; 4. Circular Wait.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Banker's Algorithm for deadlock avoidance tests whether granting a resource request leaves the system in a:
questions.explanation: Banker's Algorithm simulates resource allocation to find a safe execution sequence where every process can satisfy maximum demand without deadlock.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What happens when a process invokes the `wait()` (or `P()`) operation on a semaphore with value 0?

options.label: A
options.text: The process is blocked (placed in the semaphore waiting queue)

options.label: B
options.text: The semaphore value decrements to -1 and process continues

questions.explanation: If semaphore value `S <= 0`, executing `wait(S)` blocks the calling process until another process calls `signal(S)`.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: What is the phenomenon where the system spends more time servicing page faults and swapping pages than executing instructions?
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the sum of working sets exceeds available physical memory frames, causing continuous disk paging and CPU collapse.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Belady's Anomaly (where increasing the number of physical page frames results in an increased number of page faults) can occur in which algorithm?
questions.explanation: FIFO does not satisfy the inclusion property (stack algorithms like LRU and Optimal are immune), hence it can exhibit Belady's Anomaly.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In virtual memory paging, the hardware cache used by the Memory Management Unit (MMU) to accelerate virtual-to-physical address translation is:
questions.explanation: The TLB is high-speed associative hardware cache storing recent page-table mappings to avoid multi-level memory lookups.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A process that has finished execution but whose parent has not yet read its exit status via `wait()` system call is a:
questions.explanation: A terminated process remains a 'Zombie' in the process table holding its PID and exit code until reaped by its parent.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Unix/Linux, which system call creates an exact duplicate child process of the calling parent process?
questions.explanation: fork() duplicates the calling process, returning 0 to child and child's PID to parent. exec() replaces address space with a new program.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In language processor tools, which tool translates assembly language mnemonics into machine code object files?
questions.explanation: Assembler translates assembly code to object code; Linker combines object files and libraries; Loader loads executable into RAM.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In compiler construction, lexical analysis (Phase 1) converts high-level source text into a stream of:
questions.explanation: Lexical Analysis (Scanning) groups character streams into meaningful atomic language units called Tokens.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Given page size = 4 KB, how many bits in a 32-bit virtual address represent the page offset, and how many represent the virtual page number?

options.label: A
options.text: 12 bits offset, 20 bits virtual page number

options.label: B
options.text: 10 bits offset, 22 bits virtual page number

options.label: C
options.text: 16 bits offset, 16 bits virtual page number

options.label: D
options.text: 14 bits offset, 18 bits virtual page number

questions.explanation: Page size 4 KB = 2¹² bytes => 12 bits for Page Offset. Virtual address = 32 bits => Page Number = 32 - 12 = 20 bits.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Priority Inversion occurs when a high-priority task is indirectly blocked by a low-priority task holding a shared lock. It is resolved by:
questions.explanation: Under Priority Inheritance, the low-priority task temporarily inherits the priority of the highest-priority task waiting on its lock.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Round Robin CPU scheduling, if the Time Quantum (q) is chosen to be extremely large (larger than the longest burst time), the algorithm degenerates into:
questions.explanation: When time quantum q -> ∞, each process runs to completion on its first dispatch, exactly matching FCFS scheduling.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Which layer of the OSI 7-layer reference model is responsible for end-to-end process-to-process communication, error recovery, and flow control?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) ensures end-to-end process-to-process delivery (ports, segmentation, flow control, reliability).

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Routers operate primarily at which layer of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Routers operate at Network Layer (Layer 3) inspecting IP packet headers; Switches operate at Layer 2 (MAC); Hubs at Layer 1.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) is an error detection code standardly implemented in which network layer?
questions.explanation: CRC operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2), appending a frame check sequence (FCS) using binary polynomial division.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In CSMA/CD (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection) used in traditional Ethernet, what protocol resolves packet collisions?
questions.explanation: When a collision is detected, stations jam the channel and wait for a random slot `r ∈ [0, 2^k - 1]` using Exponential Backoff.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the broadcast address for the IPv4 subnet 192.168.10.0/24?
questions.explanation: In a /24 subnet (mask 255.255.255.0), the host bits are all 1s (255), giving the directed broadcast address 192.168.10.255.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: An organization is assigned IP network 200.100.50.0/24. If they require 4 equal subnets, what is the new subnet mask and maximum usable hosts per subnet?
questions.explanation: 4 subnets require borrowing 2 bits: /24 + 2 = /26 (mask 255.255.255.192). Host bits = 32 - 26 = 6 => Usable hosts = 2⁶ - 2 = 62 hosts.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: In TCP connection establishment, what is the correct 3-way handshake sequence exchanged between Client and Server?
questions.explanation: TCP 3-way handshake: Client sends SYN -> Server responds with SYN-ACK -> Client sends ACK. Connection is now ESTABLISHED.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which transport layer protocol is connectionless, unreliable (best-effort), and suitable for real-time video streaming and VoIP?
questions.explanation: UDP has minimal 8-byte header overhead with no retransmissions or handshake, making it ideal for low-latency streaming and DNS.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What protocol resolves an IP address into its corresponding physical hardware MAC address on a local area network?
questions.explanation: ARP broadcasts an IP address to learn the target host's 48-bit MAC address; RARP resolves MAC to IP.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: The Count-to-Infinity problem is a known routing instability vulnerability associated with which routing algorithm?
questions.explanation: Distance Vector algorithms suffer from slow convergence upon link failure (Count-to-Infinity), mitigated by split horizon and poison reverse.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which application layer protocol standardly uses well-known TCP Port 25 for sending emails across mail transfer agents?
questions.explanation: SMTP uses Port 25 (or 587) for sending email; POP3 uses Port 110; IMAP uses Port 143.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In a Sliding Window protocol, if the sender window size is W, what is the maximum link utilization in Stop-and-Wait protocol where W = 1?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 / (1 + 2a), where a = Propagation Time / Transmission Time

questions.explanation: Utilization $\eta$ = Transmission Time / (Transmission Time + 2 * Propagation Time) = 1 / (1 + 2a), where a = $T_p / T_t$.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the loopback IPv4 address reserved for testing internal network protocol stacks on a local host?
questions.explanation: The entire 127.0.0.0/8 block is reserved for loopback; 127.0.0.1 standardly points to localhost.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which ICMP message type is returned by intermediate routers when an IP packet's Time-to-Live (TTL) field reaches zero?
questions.explanation: When TTL decrements to 0, the router drops the packet and responds with an ICMP Time Exceeded message (basis for `traceroute`).

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which transmission medium utilizes total internal reflection of light pulses through silica glass strands for ultra-high-speed data transmission?
questions.explanation: Fiber optic cables transmit light modulated signals via total internal reflection across a silica glass core, offering immune EMI and gigabit speeds.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Which classic Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model follows a strictly sequential phase-by-phase progression where each phase must finish before the next begins?
questions.explanation: The Waterfall model (Winston Royce) is a linear-sequential lifecycle with distinct phases: Requirements -> Design -> Implementation -> Testing -> Maintenance.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Barry Boehm's Spiral Model is particularly suited for large, high-risk projects because every iteration explicitly incorporates:
questions.explanation: The Spiral Model is risk-driven, combining prototyping with iterative development; each spiral quadrant conducts explicit risk assessment.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In White-Box testing, McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity V(G) for a control flow graph with E edges, N nodes, and P connected components is calculated as:
questions.explanation: McCabe's formula: V(G) = E - N + 2P (or Predicate Nodes + 1 for single component), giving the count of linearly independent basis paths.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: A testing technique where input domain values are divided into classes from which test test cases are derived assuming all values in a class behave identically is:
questions.explanation: Equivalence Partitioning divides inputs into valid and invalid equivalence classes; Boundary Value Analysis focuses on boundary limits (min, max).

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which Gang of Four (GoF) design pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it?
questions.explanation: Singleton restricts instantiation of a class to one single object, using a private constructor and a static instance getter method.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: The Observer design pattern establishes which type of dependency between objects?

options.label: A
options.text: One-to-many dependency where state changes notify all dependents automatically

questions.explanation: Observer defines a one-to-many subscription model: when the Subject changes state, all registered Observers are automatically notified.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In UML class modeling, a solid line with a hollow diamond at the owner end represents which relationship?
questions.explanation: Hollow diamond = Shared Aggregation (parts can exist without container); Filled black diamond = Composition (parts destroyed with container).

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which UML diagram models the temporal sequence of messages exchanged between interacting lifeline objects over time?
questions.explanation: Sequence diagrams visualize dynamic runtime interactions, showing lifelines, activation bars, and chronological message flow.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Agile Scrum methodology, what is the fixed time-boxed development cycle (typically 2 to 4 weeks) called?
questions.explanation: A Sprint is a repeatable, time-boxed development period (usually 2–4 weeks) during which a Potentially Shippable Product Increment is built.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Software architecture principles recommend designing system modules with:
questions.explanation: Good software modularity mandates High Cohesion (elements within a module are closely focused) and Low Coupling (minimal inter-module dependency).

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What type of maintenance is performed to adapt software to changes in external environments (new OS, new database, hardware upgrade)?
questions.explanation: Adaptive maintenance modifies software to interface with changing environments; Corrective fixes bugs; Perfective enhances features.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In the Capability Maturity Model (CMM), what is the highest process maturity level (Level 5)?
questions.explanation: CMM Levels: 1. Initial; 2. Repeatable; 3. Defined; 4. Managed; 5. Optimizing (continuous process improvement and innovation).

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Regression Testing is executed after code modification primarily to:

options.label: A
options.text: Ensure that code changes have not introduced new defects into existing working features

questions.explanation: Regression testing re-runs previous test suites to verify that bug fixes or updates haven't broken existing functional capabilities.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In UML Use Case diagrams, what relationship is used when a base use case unconditionally incorporates the behavior of another use case?
questions.explanation: `<<include>>` indicates mandatory inclusion of sub-behavior; `<<extend>>` indicates optional conditional extension behavior.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which SOLID design principle states that software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification?
questions.explanation: Bertrand Meyer's Open/Closed Principle mandates that class behaviors should be extensible via inheritance or interfaces without altering source code.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Which HTML5 semantic element is intended to encapsulate autonomous, self-contained content such as a blog post or news story?
questions.explanation: HTML5 `<article>` represents independent, self-contained content distributable or reusable independently (e.g. forum post, news report).

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In the standard CSS Box Model, what is the order of areas from innermost to outermost?
questions.explanation: Innermost is Content, enclosed by Padding (space inside border), then Border, and finally Margin (transparent space outside border).

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: When `box-sizing: border-box` is declared in CSS, what does an element's specified `width` include?
questions.explanation: `border-box` includes padding and borders in the element's total width and height calculation, preventing layout overflows.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In JavaScript (ES6), how do variables declared with `const` differ from those declared with `let`?

options.label: A
options.text: const variables cannot be reassigned; let variables can be reassigned

options.label: B
options.text: const has function scope; let has block scope

options.label: C
options.text: const variables are hoisted with assignment

questions.explanation: Both `let` and `const` are block-scoped; `let` allows reassignment while `const` establishes an immutable variable identifier binding.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the return value of the expression `typeof null` in standard JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Due to a historic bug in JS's initial implementation where object tags were 000, `typeof null` evaluates to the string `"object"`.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the equality comparison result of `0 == '0'` and `0 === '0'` in JavaScript respectively?
questions.explanation: `==` performs type coercion converting string '0' to number 0 (true); `===` checks both type and value without coercion (number vs string = false).

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: A JavaScript closure is created when:

options.label: A
options.text: An inner function retains access to outer lexical environment variables even after outer function execution finishes

options.label: B
options.text: A function is called asynchronously with setTimeout

options.label: C
options.text: A class method is bound to this

questions.explanation: A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical state.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In RESTful API architectural design, which HTTP method is standardly used to modify an existing resource partially?
questions.explanation: PUT replaces the entire resource representation; PATCH applies partial modifications to an existing resource.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which HTTP status code range indicates a client-side error (e.g., 404 Not Found, 401 Unauthorized)?
questions.explanation: 1xx: Informational; 2xx: Success; 3xx: Redirection; 4xx: Client Error; 5xx: Server Error.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) data format does NOT natively support which data type?
questions.explanation: JSON natively supports only: string, number, object, array, boolean, and null. Dates are represented as ISO strings; functions are unsupported.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) web vulnerability is executed by:

options.label: A
options.text: Injecting malicious client-side JavaScript scripts into web pages viewed by other users

questions.explanation: XSS occurs when unvalidated user input is rendered in the browser, executing malicious JavaScript to steal cookies and hijack sessions.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What is the primary countermeasure against SQL Injection attacks in web applications?
questions.explanation: Prepared Statements with parameterized queries ensure that user input is treated strictly as data literals, never executable SQL commands.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks are standardly prevented by:

options.label: A
options.text: Anti-CSRF synchronizer tokens and SameSite cookie attributes

questions.explanation: Anti-CSRF unique tokens validate that state-changing requests originated from the genuine application UI; SameSite cookies block third-party transmission.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In the JavaScript asynchronous event loop, in what order are execution queues serviced after call stack completion?
questions.explanation: When the call stack empties, the event loop drains all pending Microtasks (Promise handlers, queueMicrotask) before picking the next Macrotask.

questions.subject: Web Technologies
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Which CSS property is used in Flexbox layout to align flex items along the main axis?
questions.explanation: `justify-content` aligns items along the main axis (flex-start, center, space-between); `align-items` aligns along the cross axis.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: In Symmetric-Key Cryptography, how many secret keys are utilized for encryption and decryption?

options.label: B
options.text: Two mathematically paired keys (public and private)

questions.explanation: Symmetric cryptography (e.g. AES, DES) uses one identical shared key for both encryption and decryption.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: The RSA public-key cryptographic algorithm derives its mathematical security from the computational hardness of:

options.label: A
options.text: Factoring large composite numbers into prime factors

options.label: B
options.text: Discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves

questions.explanation: RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman) relies on the integer factorization problem: multiplying two large primes is easy, but factoring their product is computationally infeasible.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What property of cryptographic hash functions (like SHA-256) guarantees that two different inputs cannot produce the identical hash digest?
questions.explanation: Collision Resistance ensures it is computationally infeasible to find any two distinct messages x and y such that hash(x) == hash(y).

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: To create an authentic Digital Signature for a message, the sender encrypts the document hash using:
questions.explanation: Digital signatures are generated using the Sender's Private Key (guaranteeing non-repudiation and authenticity), verified by anyone using Sender's Public Key.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Cloud Computing service models, Google Docs and Microsoft 365 are canonical examples of:
questions.explanation: SaaS delivers fully operational end-user applications over the web; PaaS delivers runtime dev environments; IaaS delivers VMs, storage, and networks.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: How do OS-level Containers (e.g., Docker) differ fundamentally from traditional Hypervisor Virtual Machines (VMs)?

options.label: A
options.text: Containers share the host OS kernel and package only user-space binaries and libraries

options.label: B
options.text: Containers require a complete guest operating system

options.label: C
options.text: VMs are lighter and boot faster than containers

questions.explanation: Docker containers share the host kernel via cgroups and namespaces, making them lightweight and fast compared to VMs carrying full guest OS kernels.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Machine Learning, training a model on unlabelled data to discover hidden clusters and patterns without target output labels is called:
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning (e.g., K-Means clustering, PCA) finds inherent groupings in unlabelled datasets; Supervised learning trains on labeled (X, y) pairs.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Artificial Neural Networks, the non-linear mathematical function that decides whether a neuron should fire is called an:
questions.explanation: Activation functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh) introduce non-linearity into neural networks, enabling them to learn complex non-linear decision boundaries.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Blockchain technology, how are blocks cryptographically chained together to make history tamper-evident?

options.label: A
options.text: Each block contains the cryptographic hash of the previous block's header

options.label: B
options.text: Blocks are linked via physical Ethernet cables

options.label: C
options.text: A central database administrator signs all blocks

options.label: D
options.text: Blocks are indexed by row count

questions.explanation: Every block references `Previous_Block_Hash`. Altering any past block invalidates all subsequent block hashes across the distributed ledger.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, which lightweight publish-subscribe messaging protocol designed for constrained low-bandwidth devices is standardly used?
questions.explanation: MQTT is a minimal publish/subscribe protocol with tiny 2-byte packet headers, ideal for battery-operated IoT sensors over cellular/satellite links.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: PYQ
questions.text: The CIA Triad constitutes the foundational pillars of information security. What does CIA stand for?
questions.explanation: Confidentiality (preventing unauthorized reading), Integrity (preventing unauthorized modification), and Availability (ensuring authorized access when needed).

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: What type of cryptographic attack precomputes millions of password hashes into indexed lookup tables to reverse password digests rapidly?
questions.explanation: Rainbow tables trade space for time by storing precomputed hash chains; defended by adding unique random Salt to passwords before hashing.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In Kubernetes container orchestration architecture, what is the smallest, basic deployable compute unit that encapsulates one or more containers?
questions.explanation: A Pod represents a single instance of a running process in Kubernetes, sharing network namespace (IP) and storage volumes among its containers.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: In machine learning evaluation metrics, what is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall called?
questions.explanation: F1-Score = 2 * (Precision * Recall) / (Precision + Recall), providing an balanced evaluation metric especially on imbalanced datasets.

questions.subject: Information Security
questions.label: expected
questions.text: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange allows two parties to establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel without transmitting the key. It is vulnerable to:
questions.explanation: Classic Diffie-Hellman does not authenticate the communicating parties; an active attacker can intercept and establish independent keys with both sides (MitM).
